papers.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Abstract ChronoReplay mitigates interface lock-in in spatial vision-language models by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision chronologically, improving cross-task transfer and enabling efficient inference-time evidence selection.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Training a spatial VLM to answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. When post-training emphasizes one readout, improvements can therefore concentrate on that interface while transfer to others remains weak or even degrades; we call this observed specialization interface lock-in. ChronoReplay addresses it by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes, retaining source-native targets, and balancing supervision across families. Under the same observation access, a single ChronoReplay checkpoint improves OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench together, including a 13.41-point gain on OST-Bench, and achieves the highest three-benchmark mean among the supervision settings compared here. Same-data controls further separate the ingredients of this transfer: answer serialization redistributes gains across OST and UCS, family-balanced learning improves over ordinary joint SFT and natural turn weighting, and chronological replay exceeds a shifted-order control by about 2.41 OST points across two paired seeds. Adaptive frame selection then changes evidence access while keeping the trained model fixed, providing an additional inference-time gain at lower visual cost. Streaming spatial performance depends on what distinctions supervision preserves, how heterogeneous histories are organized during learning, and what causal evidence inference makes available at test time.

ru.title: Учим модель помнить пространство во времени, а не в одном ответе
ru.desc: Статья показывает, что при дообучении пространственных VLM (vision-language models) модель часто улучшается только по одному типу вопросов, например по направлению объекта, и почти не переносит навык на другие, что авторы называют interface lock-in. Предлагается метод ChronoReplay, который воспроизводит разнородные пространственные данные в хронологическом порядке эпизодов, сохраняет исходные целевые метки и балансирует supervision между семействами задач. Единый checkpoint, обученный так, улучшает сразу несколько бенчмарков, включая OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench и UCS-Bench, с приростом 13.41 на OST-Bench. Дополнительно адаптивный отбор кадров на этапе inference даёт прирост качества при меньших вычислительных затратах на визуальную часть.

en.title: ChronoReplay: Breaking Free from Interface Lock-In in Spatial VLMs
en.desc: ChronoReplay is a method designed to reduce the problem of interface lock-in in spatial vision-language models (VLMs) by using a chronological approach to replay different types of spatial supervision. This technique enhances the model's ability to transfer knowledge across various tasks and improves the selection of evidence during inference. By balancing supervision across different categories and retaining original target formats, ChronoReplay allows for better performance on multiple benchmarks. The results show significant improvements in task performance, demonstrating that how supervision is structured and accessed can greatly influence a model's effectiveness.

zh.title: ChronoReplay：打破接口锁定，提升模型迁移能力
zh.desc: ChronoReplay 是一种方法，用于减少空间视觉语言模型中的接口锁定现象。它通过按时间顺序重放不同类型的空间监督，来改善跨任务的迁移能力，并提高推理时证据选择的效率。研究表明，强调某一特定输出的训练可能导致模型在其他任务上的性能下降，这种现象被称为接口锁定。ChronoReplay 通过平衡不同类型的监督和保留源目标，成功地提升了多个基准测试的表现。

papers.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract Hy-Nomas is a video world model that uses causal attention and structured captions to follow multi-turn text and camera instructions while preserving interaction history.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed by diffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research on interactive world generation.

ru.title: Интерактивный мир из видео, который помнит историю и слушает команды
ru.desc: В статье представлена Hy-Nomas — модель мира для видео (video world model) с 8B диффузионным бэкбоном, которая выполняет многоходовые текстовые инструкции и непрерывное управление камерой. Ключевая идея — согласование структурированных описаний видео с каузальным вниманием (causal attention) с учётом действий: описательный контекст доступен между сегментами, а инструкции действий ограничены своими временными окнами. Модуль Prompt Enhancer на основе vision-language модели переводит запросы пользователя и мультимодальную историю взаимодействия в структурированные условия для следующего сегмента. Обучение проходит по многоэтапному curriculum, завершается дистилляцией диффузии, и модель превосходит существующие world models по оценке людей.

en.title: Hy-Nomas: Mastering Interactive Video Generation with Causal Attention
en.desc: Hy-Nomas is an advanced video world model designed to understand and execute multi-turn text and camera commands while keeping track of previous interactions. It utilizes an 8B diffusion backbone to generate video segments that adapt to user inputs and maintain a history of actions. The model employs causal attention to ensure that relevant context is preserved across different segments, while also managing action instructions within specific time frames. By integrating a vision-language Prompt Enhancer, Hy-Nomas effectively translates user requests into structured conditions, demonstrating superior performance in human evaluations compared to existing models.

zh.title: Hy-Nomas：智能视频世界模型的未来
zh.desc: Hy-Nomas是一种视频世界模型，利用因果注意力和结构化字幕来跟踪多轮文本和相机指令，同时保留交互历史。该模型能够在多个交互回合中支持自由形式的文本指令和连续的相机控制。Hy-Nomas生成的可变长度片段基于当前输入和缓存的历史信息，并通过结构化视频字幕与动作感知因果注意力相结合，确保描述性上下文在片段间可访问。经过人类评估，Hy-Nomas在性能上优于现有的世界模型，并提供了模型权重、代码和基准，以支持可重复的交互世界生成研究。

papers.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
papers.abstract: Abstract Rollback improves robot policies by using world models to rewind to past decisions, explore counterfactual actions, and generate fine-grained supervision, while continuously refining dynamics via real-world feedback.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.

ru.title: Перематываем назад, чтобы робот научился лучше: контрфактуальные миры вместо дорогого реального опыта
ru.desc: Статья предлагает метод Rollback для улучшения политик роботов, в котором world model используется не просто как симулятор, а как инструмент контрфактуальных рассуждений. Система откатывается к критическим точкам принятия решений, пробует альтернативные действия и сравнивает их исходы, что позволяет присвоить успех отдельным решениям без отдельной value model. Модель мира непрерывно уточняется реальными переходами через lightweight LoRA, что реализует идею test-time physics grounding. В экспериментах на трёх реальных задачах метод улучшил success rate на 10-12% относительно сильнейшего baseline и на некоторых задачах превзошёл средний результат людей за 8 часов обучения.

en.title: Rollback: Enhancing Robot Learning through Counterfactual Exploration
en.desc: The paper introduces Rollback, a novel approach that enhances robot policies by utilizing world models to revisit past decisions and explore alternative actions. This method transforms world models from simple simulators into powerful tools for counterfactual reasoning, allowing robots to analyze the outcomes of different choices. By integrating real-world feedback, Rollback continuously refines the dynamics of the world model, creating a feedback loop that improves policy performance. Experiments demonstrate that Rollback significantly increases success rates in various tasks, outperforming traditional methods and even human players after limited training.

zh.title: Rollback：机器人策略的反事实引擎
zh.desc: Rollback是一种通过世界模型改进机器人策略的方法。它可以回溯到过去的决策点，探索不同的行动选择，并生成细粒度的监督信息，同时通过现实世界的反馈不断优化动态模型。与传统的世界模型方法不同，Rollback将世界模型从被动的模拟器转变为反事实引擎，能够对比不同决策的结果，从而更好地理解成功的原因。实验表明，Rollback在多个真实世界任务中显著提高了成功率，且训练过程中的改进更加稳定。

papers.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract ThinkWorld improves robotic generalization by representing actions as dynamics chains and using world imagination to learn from unlabeled human videos.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

ru.title: Учимся у людей по видео: роботы думают о динамике мира
ru.desc: Статья представляет ThinkWorld — фреймворк для Vision-Language-Action (VLA) моделей, который улучшает обобщение в робототехнике. Каждое действие представляется как Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), последовательность дискретных motion-токенов, описывающих промежуточную динамику от текущего состояния мира к будущему. Модель сначала обучается на демонстрациях с разметкой действий, затем с помощью reinforcement learning с world imagination усиливает те CoD, которые лучше предсказывают наблюдаемый исход. Это позволяет использовать видео человека без разметки действий, и в экспериментах достигается хороший перенос с человека на робота и обобщение на новые задачи и среды.

en.title: Empowering Robots with Human-Like Learning through Dynamics Chains
en.desc: ThinkWorld is a machine learning framework that enhances how robots learn to perform tasks by using human videos instead of just labeled action demonstrations. It introduces the concept of Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), which represents actions as sequences of motion tokens that connect current states to future outcomes. By leveraging reinforcement learning and world imagination, ThinkWorld allows robots to learn from the dynamics observed in human videos, even when those videos lack explicit action labels. This approach enables better generalization to new tasks and environments, improving the transfer of knowledge from humans to robots.

zh.title: ThinkWorld：提升机器人泛化能力的新框架
zh.desc: ThinkWorld 是一种改进机器人泛化能力的框架，它通过将动作表示为动态链，并利用世界想象从未标记的人类视频中学习。该方法解决了从人类视频学习时可扩展数据与明确动作基础之间的权衡。ThinkWorld 使用动态链（CoD）来表示每个动作，捕捉当前世界与未来状态之间的中间动态，并通过强化学习来增强这一过程。实验表明，ThinkWorld 能够有效地实现人类与机器人之间的知识转移，并在未见过的任务和环境中表现出强大的泛化能力。

papers.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
papers.abstract: Abstract Executable code representations of video content improve reasoning and reconstruction over natural language, yet current multimodal models still struggle to generate faithful code captions for complex temporal dynamics.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. In this work, we explore Code as Video Caption, a paradigm where executable programs serve as a complementary representation of visual content through graphical primitives, layout rules, and functions of time. To examine whether code captions effectively preserve video information, we compare them with natural language captions on downstream question answering and video reconstruction tasks. Our results show that code captions achieve superior reasoning accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Despite these advantages, realizing the potential of code captioning depends on whether current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate faithful code captions. To systematically assess this capability, we introduce CodeCap-Bench, which comprises 323 videos spanning five categories of structured 2D content, along with fine-grained annotations and a multi-level evaluation framework. Extensive experiments reveal that while leading proprietary MLLMs demonstrate promising code captioning capabilities, they still struggle to faithfully capture complex temporal dynamics, with open-source models lagging substantially behind.

ru.title: Код вместо слов: видео лучше описывать программой, а не текстом
ru.desc: Статья предлагает подход Code as Video Caption, в котором описание видео задаётся исполняемым кодом: графическими примитивами, правилами компоновки и функциями времени, а не длинным текстом на естественном языке. Авторы показывают, что такие код-подписи дают более высокую точность ответов на вопросы и лучшее качество восстановления видео по сравнению с текстовыми подписями. Для оценки способности MLLM генерировать такой код введён бенчмарк CodeCap-Bench из 323 видео в пяти категориях структурированного 2D-контента с детальной разметкой и многоуровневой системой оценки. Эксперименты показывают, что ведущие проприетарные модели справляются с задачей неплохо, но всё ещё плохо передают сложную временную динамику, а open-source модели заметно отстают.

en.title: Unlocking Video Understanding with Code Captions
en.desc: This paper introduces a new approach to video captioning called Code as Video Caption, where executable code is used to represent video content instead of traditional natural language descriptions. The authors argue that code can more accurately capture complex spatial structures and temporal dynamics in videos, leading to better reasoning and reconstruction outcomes. They present a benchmark called CodeCap-Bench, which includes a diverse set of videos and detailed annotations to evaluate the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in generating code captions. The findings indicate that while some MLLMs show promise in code captioning, they still face challenges in accurately representing intricate temporal aspects of video content.

zh.title: 代码标题：视频内容的新表达方式
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了使用可执行代码作为视频内容的描述，以提高对复杂时间动态的推理和重建能力。传统的多模态模型在生成准确的自然语言视频标题时面临挑战，尤其是在表达细致的空间结构和时间动态方面。研究表明，代码标题在视频信息的保留上优于自然语言标题，尤其在问答和视频重建任务中表现出更高的推理准确性和重建保真度。为了评估当前多模态大语言模型生成代码标题的能力，作者提出了CodeCap-Bench，这是一个包含323个视频的评估框架，涵盖了五类结构化2D内容。

papers.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Abstract Large-scale evaluation reveals that dedicated memory systems often underperform naive retrieval-augmented generation, introducing a framework of memory benefit and memory tax to assess net value.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value. Taking RAG as a reference, we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termed memory benefit and memory tax. These gains and losses arise because memory process changes how the raw information is organized and accessed. We view such changes as the double-edged deviations from the raw history. They are originally designed and introduced to benefit the task, for example by reorganizing facts or distilling preferences, but some may also remove or obscure evidence, giving rise to memory tax. Since memory benefit reflects the expected gains of its design, we then focus more on the overlooked memory tax, study how it arises from the system and evaluation side, and generalize the concept to more application scenarios of memory. We hope the notion of memory tax can provide a new lens and shift more attention from standalone performance to the net value of memory, informing more reliable memory designs and evaluations. We will open-source the code and results to the community. Project Page: https://hexuan21.github.io/MemoryTax/

ru.title: Память агента должна окупаться: учитывайте не только выигрыш, но и налог на память
ru.desc: В статье показано, что специализированные системы памяти для LLM-агентов часто уступают наивному RAG, то есть прямому поиску по сырой истории диалога. Авторы вводят понятия memory benefit (выигрыш от организации памяти) и memory tax (потери, которые память вносит, удаляя или искажая доказательства). Оценка проводилась на нескольких бенчмарках и разных backbone-моделях, а основное внимание уделено изучению memory tax, его источников и обобщению на другие сценарии. Цель работы — перевести фокус с отдельной производительности на чистую ценность памяти для более надежного дизайна и оценки.

en.title: Understanding Memory: Balancing Benefits and Costs in AI
en.desc: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of dedicated memory systems in machine learning, particularly in long-horizon agents. It introduces the concepts of 'memory benefit' and 'memory tax' to analyze the advantages and disadvantages of using memory compared to direct retrieval methods. The findings suggest that many memory systems do not perform as well as naive retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), indicating a negative net value. The authors emphasize the importance of understanding memory tax to improve memory system designs and evaluations in future applications.

zh.title: 重新审视记忆系统的价值
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了在机器学习中使用记忆系统的价值，特别是在长时间跨度的智能体中。研究发现，专用的记忆系统在许多情况下表现不如简单的检索增强生成（RAG），这表明它们的净价值可能是负的。论文提出了“记忆收益”和“记忆税”的框架，用于评估记忆系统的优缺点，强调了记忆过程如何影响信息的组织和访问。作者希望通过关注记忆税的概念，促使人们重新审视记忆的设计和评估，以实现更可靠的记忆系统。

papers.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
papers.abstract: Abstract LociArt enables precise local video stylization with region-style control and temporal consistency via a generative refinement network, automated dataset construction, and a dedicated benchmark.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video stylization typically transforms entire scenes, while local artistic editing requires precise region--style association, spatial control, and temporal consistency. We introduce LociArt, a unified paradigm for free-style local video stylization that explicitly specifies where to stylize and what style to apply while preserving non-target content. At its core, GRNStyle builds on Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) and introduces a polar style-aware mask that embeds style identities as equal-norm directions within selected regions. Complementary representation--geometry conditioning combines encoded mask features with raw-mask spatial support, integrating spatiotemporal context with geometric control. To provide paired supervision, we develop an automated pipeline combining global stylization, video object removal, matting, and compositing, and construct the LociArt-100K Dataset with 100K local stylization pairs. We further establish the LociArt Benchmark, comprising 80 source videos and 84 target masks covering 168 foreground/background stylization cases, with a Style Prototype Similarity (SPS) evaluation scheme for regional style quality and complementary measures of non-target preservation and temporal consistency. Experiments show that GRNStyle outperforms existing methods in regional style quality and spatial control while maintaining strong temporal consistency. Qualitative examples further illustrate joint stylization of multiple regions with the same or different learned styles, despite training only on single-region, single-style pairs. Together, these components provide a unified foundation for learning and evaluating controllable local video stylization. Project page: https://higherhu.github.io/lociart/.
affiliations: Xian University of Electronic Science and Technology

ru.title: Стилизуй только нужное: точная локальная стилизация видео
ru.desc: Статья представляет LociArt — подход к локальной стилизации видео, который задаёт, где и каким стилем применять эффект, сохраняя остальной контент. Ядро метода GRNStyle построено на Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) и использует полярную style-aware маску, кодирующую стили как направления равной нормы внутри выбранных областей, плюс условие на представление и геометрию. Авторы создают автоматический пайплайн для получения парных данных и датасет LociArt-100K из 100 тысяч пар, а также бенчмарк LociArt с метрикой Style Prototype Similarity (SPS). Эксперименты показывают превосходство над существующими методами по качеству регионального стиля и пространственному контролю при сильной временной согласованности, включая совместную стилизацию нескольких регионов, хотя обучение велось только на парах с одним регионом и одним стилем.

en.title: Precision in Local Video Stylization with LociArt
en.desc: LociArt is a novel approach for local video stylization that allows users to specify which regions of a video to stylize and what artistic style to apply, while keeping the rest of the content unchanged. It utilizes a Generative Refinement Network (GRN) that incorporates a polar style-aware mask to manage style identities within selected areas. The method also integrates spatiotemporal context with geometric control through complementary representation-geometry conditioning. To support its development, LociArt includes an automated dataset construction process and a benchmark for evaluating the quality of regional stylization and temporal consistency across various video scenarios.

zh.title: 局部视频风格化的新方法
zh.desc: LociArt 是一种新方法，可以精确地对视频进行局部风格化，并且允许用户控制不同区域的风格。它使用生成性细化网络（GRN）来确保风格的一致性和空间控制，同时保留非目标内容。通过自动化的数据集构建，LociArt 创建了一个包含 10 万对局部风格化样本的数据集，并建立了 LociArt 基准测试，以评估风格质量和时间一致性。实验结果表明，LociArt 在区域风格质量和空间控制方面优于现有方法。

papers.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Abstract HABIT-Bench evaluates whether LLM agent memory systems can infer implicit user habits from sparse dialogue evidence and apply them correctly across long-term interactions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies. Retaining past interactions alone does not ensure that agents can infer habits and apply them appropriately. We introduce HABIT-Bench to evaluate how well agent memory systems infer habits from weak evidence and apply them to later requests. We construct synthetic user histories from task-oriented dialogue data and controlled habit graphs. The histories span hundreds of sessions across food, finance, software, and travel. Four-choice tasks assess agents' ability to infer user habits and apply them appropriately. They include temporary exceptions, changes in habits, and suggestions that users have not accepted. Sampled tasks undergo independent human review. We evaluate eight memory methods with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.3-Flash. The best-performing memory method achieves 33.61\% macro accuracy across the four domains. Performance remains limited even when annotated evidence is supplied directly. These results expose a persistent gap between access to past interactions and the ability to infer and appropriately use user habits.

ru.title: Хранить историю мало: агенты должны понимать привычки пользователя
ru.desc: В статье представлен HABIT-Bench, новый бенчмарк для оценки того, способны ли системы памяти LLM-агентов выводить неявные привычки пользователя из разрозненных данных диалогов. Синтетические истории пользователей строятся на основе датасетов task-oriented диалогов и контролируемых графов привычек в областях еды, финансов, ПО и путешествий. Задачи с четырьмя вариантами ответа проверяют умение учитывать временные исключения, изменения привычек и непринятые рекомендации. Результаты восьми методов памяти показывают, что лучший достигает лишь 33.61% macro accuracy, и даже при подаче размеченных доказательств качество остается низким, что выявляет разрыв между доступом к истории и реальным использованием привычек.

en.title: Evaluating Memory Systems for Inferring User Habits in LLMs
en.desc: The paper introduces HABIT-Bench, a framework designed to evaluate how well large language model (LLM) agents can infer user habits from sparse dialogue evidence during long-term interactions. It highlights that users often reveal their habits through their choices, but individual observations may not provide complete information about these habits. The study constructs synthetic user histories and assesses agents' abilities to apply inferred habits in various contexts, including exceptions and changes. Results show that even with access to past interactions, agents struggle to accurately infer and utilize user habits, indicating a significant gap in current memory systems.

zh.title: 评估记忆系统推断用户习惯的能力
zh.desc: HABIT-Bench 是一个评估大型语言模型（LLM）代理记忆系统的工具，旨在判断它们能否从稀疏的对话证据中推断出用户的隐含习惯，并在长期交互中正确应用这些习惯。用户在与 LLM 代理的长期互动中，通过选择和行动透露出习惯，这些习惯包含了隐含的用户信息。尽管保留过去的互动记录，但这并不能保证代理能够准确推断习惯并适当地应用。我们构建了合成用户历史记录，并通过四个领域的任务评估代理推断用户习惯的能力。

papers.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract The Trinity framework recursively improves multimodal agents by organizing tasks into a capability tree, generating simulated training worlds, and routing specialized harness modules to boost performance on diverse benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.

ru.title: Общие способности важнее формы задачи: агенты учатся, переиспользуя навыки
ru.desc: В статье представлен фреймворк Trinity, который рекурсивно улучшает мультимодальных AI-агентов: задачи организуются в дерево способностей, а Creator генерирует упрощённые верифицируемые симулированные миры для обучения. Роль Explorer постепенно эволюционирует переиспользуемые модули (Harness tree), а Capability-Aware Harness Router выбирает подходящую конфигурацию модулей по публичной информации о задаче. Подход основан на идее, что задачи разных модальностей могут требовать одних и тех же базовых способностей. Эксперименты показывают прирост средней производительности на 34 пункта на обучающих бенчмарках и на 26 пунктов на невидимых, включая две реальные embodied-задачи.

en.title: Empowering Multimodal Agents through Capability-Driven Evolution
en.desc: The Trinity framework enhances multimodal agents by structuring tasks into a capability tree, which allows for better organization and performance improvement. It generates simulated training environments that help agents learn and adapt to various tasks more efficiently. By focusing on shared underlying capabilities rather than surface-level task differences, Trinity enables a more streamlined approach to harness evolution and task organization. This results in specialized harness modules that significantly boost performance across multiple benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of capability-driven learning.

zh.title: Trinity框架：提升多模态智能体的能力
zh.desc: Trinity框架通过将任务组织成能力树，递归地提升多模态智能体的性能。它生成模拟训练环境，并通过专门的Harness模块来增强在不同基准上的表现。该框架的关键在于不同模态和表面形式的任务可以共享相同的能力需求，从而实现更高效的任务组织。最终，Trinity框架使得多模态智能体在多项训练基准上平均提升了34分，在未见基准上提升了26分。

papers.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
papers.abstract: Abstract PDRVLA improves robot action generation by integrating a lightweight physical dynamics module that predicts future visual features with world-model supervision, avoiding online video generation latency.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

ru.title: Роботы понимают физику без задержек: предсказываем будущее, а не рендерим видео
ru.desc: Статья представляет PDRVLA, улучшение моделей VLA (Vision-Language-Action), которые генерируют действия робота по изображениям и текстовым инструкциям. Авторы добавляют легковесный модуль физической динамики, который извлекает физические токены из признаков vision-language и предсказывает будущие RGB, глубину и оптический поток без генерации видео в реальном времени. Модуль обучается с вспомогательным надзором от замороженной предобученной video world model, а обучение использует публичные данные и аннотации подзадач и ECoT. На четырёх симуляционных бенчмарках метод показывает высокую успешность, например 99.3% на LIBERO и 93.6% на RoboTwin 2.0.

en.title: Predicting the Future: Enhancing Robot Actions with PDRVLA
en.desc: PDRVLA is a novel approach that enhances robot action generation by incorporating a lightweight physical dynamics module. This module predicts future visual features, allowing robots to understand and react to their environment more effectively without the delays caused by generating videos in real-time. By using world-model supervision, PDRVLA conditions action generation on physical tokens derived from vision-language features, improving the robot's ability to anticipate future states. The method demonstrates impressive performance across multiple simulation benchmarks, showcasing its effectiveness in real-world applications.

zh.title: 提升机器人动作生成的智能方法
zh.desc: PDRVLA是一种改进机器人动作生成的方法，它通过集成一个轻量级的物理动态模块来预测未来的视觉特征，从而避免在线视频生成的延迟。该模块利用视觉-语言特征提取物理信息，以便在不生成视频的情况下进行动作生成。PDRVLA的训练完全依赖于公开数据，并通过人机合成和子任务注释进行扩展。实验结果显示，PDRVLA在多个模拟基准测试中取得了很高的成功率，证明了其在机器人控制中的有效性。

papers.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
papers.abstract: Abstract Test-Time Memory Evolution updates external memory without changing model weights to guide scientific discovery more efficiently than test-time training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent test-time training (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient test-time adaptation method for scientific discovery. We introduce Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide subsequent discovery without updating model weights. To have a clean comparison, we evaluate TTME and TTT under the same discovery framework, replacing only the test-time adaptation method. Our evaluation shows that TTME outperforms TTT on all five mathematical tasks, while reducing computational cost by 82.8-84.6% in FLOPs and 47.7-58.4% in runtime. These results establish TTME as an effective and computationally efficient alternative to TTT in the evaluated discovery settings.

ru.title: Память вместо весов: эффективная адаптация LLM при поиске научных открытий
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME) — альтернатива Test-Time Training (TTT) для научных открытий с помощью LLM. TTME не меняет веса модели, а постоянно обновляет внешнюю память, дистиллируя накопленный опыт для направления последующего поиска. Сравнение проводилось в одной и той же среде открытий, где менялся только метод адаптации на этапе инференса. На пяти математических задачах TTME превзошёл TTT, снизив вычислительные затраты на 82.8–84.6% по FLOPs и на 47.7–58.4% по времени выполнения.

en.title: Efficient Memory Updates for Smarter Scientific Discovery
en.desc: This paper presents Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a method that updates external memory during the test phase without altering the model's weights. Unlike traditional test-time training (TTT), which incurs high computational costs for weight updates, TTME focuses on efficiently guiding scientific discovery by distilling experiences into memory. The authors demonstrate that TTME significantly outperforms TTT across various mathematical tasks while drastically reducing computational demands. This makes TTME a promising alternative for adapting models in real-time scientific applications.

zh.title: 测试时记忆演化：高效的科学发现新方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为测试时记忆演化（TTME）的方法，用于在科学发现任务中高效地更新外部记忆，而不改变模型权重。与传统的测试时训练（TTT）相比，TTME能够在保持计算效率的同时，持续提炼经验以指导后续的发现过程。研究表明，TTME在五个数学任务上均优于TTT，并且在计算成本上减少了82.8-84.6%的FLOPs和47.7-58.4%的运行时间。这使得TTME成为在评估的发现环境中，TTT的有效且计算高效的替代方案。

papers.title: MatAnyone-E: Sparse Memory Propagation for Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting
papers.abstract: Abstract MatAnyone-E accelerates high-resolution video matting by selectively applying high-resolution matching to uncertain regions and using a lightweight decoder, achieving large speedups with preserved quality.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small High-resolution video matting requires preserving fine details, such as hair strands and soft transparency, while maintaining consistency across frames. Memory-based methods achieve strong matting quality by matching current-frame features with information stored from earlier frames, but this process becomes increasingly costly as resolution grows. We present MatAnyone-E, an efficient extension of MatAnyone 2 that focuses computation where it is most needed. Our approach first performs low-resolution propagation to identify uncertain regions that require closer inspection and the memory candidates most relevant to them. It then performs high-resolution matching only for these regions using the selected memory, while reusing low-resolution matching results elsewhere. This strategy reduces both the number of locations requiring detailed matching and the amount of memory searched, while preserving the information needed to produce a complete matte. We further reduce the cost of generating high-resolution mattes with a lightweight decoder designed around measured runtime bottlenecks and trained to reproduce the original decoder's representations. Experiments show that MatAnyone-E maintains matting quality comparable to MatAnyone 2 while achieving an estimated 7.4x inference speedup and reducing peak GPU memory usage to 7.6% of the usage of MatAnyone 2 at 4K. With compilation-enabled inference on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU, it reaches 73.07 FPS at 1080p and 28.62 FPS at 4K.

ru.title: Точность там, где она нужна: быстрый матинг видео в 4K без потери качества
ru.desc: Статья представляет MatAnyone-E — ускоренную версию модели для высокопроизводительного матинга видео, которая сохраняет тонкие детали, такие как пряди волос и полупрозрачность. Метод сначала выполняет распространение на низком разрешении, чтобы найти неопределённые области и релевантные элементы памяти, а затем применяет высокоразрешающее сопоставление только к этим участкам. Для ускорения генерации масок используется облегчённый декодер, обученный воспроизводить представления исходного. По результатам экспериментов качество сопоставимо с MatAnyone 2, при этом скорость вывода возрастает примерно в 7.4 раза, а пиковое потребление памяти GPU в 4K снижается до 7.6%.

en.title: Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting with MatAnyone-E
en.desc: The paper introduces MatAnyone-E, a method that speeds up high-resolution video matting by focusing computational resources on uncertain areas that need more detail. It uses low-resolution propagation to identify these areas and selectively applies high-resolution matching only where necessary, which reduces the overall computational load. Additionally, a lightweight decoder is employed to further enhance efficiency while maintaining high-quality output. The results show significant improvements in speed and reduced memory usage compared to previous methods, making it suitable for real-time applications.

zh.title: 高效视频抠图，速度与质量兼得
zh.desc: MatAnyone-E 是一种高效的视频抠图方法，通过选择性地在不确定区域应用高分辨率匹配，并使用轻量级解码器，显著加快了处理速度，同时保持了图像质量。该方法首先进行低分辨率传播，以识别需要更仔细检查的不确定区域，并选择与之相关的记忆候选。然后，仅对这些区域进行高分辨率匹配，而在其他地方重用低分辨率匹配结果，从而减少了详细匹配所需的位置数量和搜索的内存量。实验表明，MatAnyone-E 在保持与 MatAnyone 2 相当的抠图质量的同时，实现了约 7.4 倍的推理加速，并将峰值 GPU 内存使用量降低到 MatAnyone 2 的 7.6%。

papers.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
papers.abstract: Abstract RSI Arena demonstrates that autonomous AI agents can independently train and iteratively improve language models using human feedback, with most agents achieving preference gains in a second stage despite modest benchmark improvements.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. Ten frontier models act as training agents, each starting from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. During a six-day first stage, each agent has 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 in API credit on a shared 64-GPU cluster, independently selecting data, implementing training procedures, and choosing checkpoints. We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closing a median of 76% of the base-to-Instruct gap across 12 capability benchmarks. Its human-preference rating is also close to NVIDIA Instruct after statistical adjustment for answer length and formatting. In Stage 2, each agent receives the comparison records and votes involving its Stage 1 model and is given three additional days for further training. Using NVIDIA Instruct as a common reference across the two evaluation rounds, we observe an improvement from Stage 1 to Stage 2 in the style-adjusted relative rating of eight of the ten models. We show that benchmark gains were modest, with no clear link to preference gains, while some agents encouraged longer responses and one model showed increased harmful compliance on StrongREJECT. RSI Arena provides an auditable setting for studying how human feedback can guide autonomous model development. It takes a step toward recursive self-improvement with human feedback (RSIHF), in which people help define what improvement means for the AI systems they use.

ru.title: ИИ-агенты учатся сами, а люди задают, что значит «лучше»
ru.desc: В статье представлен RSI Arena — двухэтапное исследование, в котором десять frontier-моделей выступают как автономные агенты и самостоятельно выполняют post-training языковой модели NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. На первом этапе агенты сами выбирают данные, реализуют процедуры обучения и выбирают чекпоинты при ограниченных GPU-часах и бюджете API, а затем модели оцениваются на 20 бенчмарках и через слепую оценку людей. На втором этапе агенты получают записи сравнений и голоса пользователей и дообучают свои модели, при этом предпочтения людей в основном улучшаются, тогда как прирост на бенчмарках скромный и не связан с ними напрямую. Авторы показывают, что такой подход — шаг к рекурсивному самоулучшению с обратной связью от человека (RSIHF), в котором люди помогают определить, что считать улучшением.

en.title: Empowering AI: Autonomous Learning Through Human Feedback
en.desc: RSI Arena explores how autonomous AI agents can train and enhance language models using human feedback. The study involves two stages where ten AI models independently select data and training methods to improve their performance. Despite modest improvements in benchmarks, many agents show significant gains in user preference ratings after receiving feedback. This research highlights the potential for recursive self-improvement in AI systems guided by human input.

zh.title: 自主AI代理的语言模型改进之路
zh.desc: RSI Arena展示了自主AI代理如何利用人类反馈独立训练和迭代改进语言模型。研究分为两个阶段，十个前沿模型作为训练代理，在第一阶段中独立选择数据和训练程序。经过评估，所有代理都能生成有效的助手，其中最强的模型在能力基准测试中缩小了76%的差距。第二阶段中，代理根据第一阶段的反馈进行进一步训练，观察到大多数模型在风格调整后的评分上有所提升。

papers.title: Omni-InteractScope: Benchmarking Proactive and Agentic Interaction in Continuous Omnimodal Streams
papers.abstract: Abstract Omni-InteractScope evaluates continuous audiovisual interaction reliability, revealing that current Omni-LLMs struggle with timely tool use, query-free reminders, and sustained guidance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) are increasingly expected to assist users while observing continuous audiovisual streams. However, existing evaluations provide limited insight into how reliably these models connect stream evidence and user needs to timely, sustained interventions. We introduce Omni-InteractScope, a benchmark of 1,479 human-annotated, cross-reviewed interactions with 1,790 temporal targets across eight task groups. It links input modalities, event triggers, intervention types, and user needs, covering event-timed tool invocation and query-free assistance alongside notifications, warnings, state tracking, and continuous responses. Our experimental results on the proposed benchmark reveal three critical limitations of current Omni-LLMs: (1) Timely tool invocation remains unreliable: all 12 evaluated models produce an on-time first response for at most 40\% of tool-invocation targets, and joint timing-and-tool accuracy reaches at most 32.0\%. (2) Query-free reminders remain poorly covered: all evaluated models achieve lower timely reference-target recall on query-free reminders than on explicit questions, measured on their respective target sets. Reminder recall never exceeds 23.0\%. (3) End-to-end guidance coverage remains limited: nine models cover none of the 26 guidance sequences in full, and the remaining three cover only one to three sequences each. Targeted controls further show that tool-invocation scores alone do not establish event grounding and that reminder coverage depends on response history and frequency. These findings motivate developing and evaluating streaming assistants for timely action, initiative under general user needs, and coverage of entire response sequences.

ru.title: Омни-модели пока плохо успевают помогать в реальном времени
ru.desc: Статья представляет Omni-InteractScope — новый бенчмарк из 1479 вручную размеченных взаимодействий для оценки омнимодальных LLM, которые следят за непрерывным аудио- и видеопотоком. Авторы проверяют, насколько надёжно модели вовремя вызывают инструменты, сами дают напоминания без запроса и ведут пользователя по последовательностям действий. Результаты показывают серьёзные ограничения: своевременный вызов инструментов удаётся не более чем в 40% случаев, а напоминания без запроса покрываются хуже, чем ответы на явные вопросы. Авторы делают вывод, что нужны потоковые ассистенты, способные действовать вовремя, проявлять инициативу и доводить ответы до конца.

en.title: Enhancing Reliability in Audiovisual Interaction with Omni-LLMs
en.desc: The paper introduces Omni-InteractScope, a benchmark designed to evaluate the reliability of Omni-LLMs in continuous audiovisual interactions. It highlights that current models struggle with timely tool usage, effective query-free reminders, and providing sustained guidance to users. The study reveals that these models only achieve a maximum of 40% on-time responses for tool invocation and have low recall rates for query-free reminders. Overall, the findings emphasize the need for improved streaming assistants that can better meet user needs through timely and comprehensive responses.

zh.title: 提升Omni-LLMs的交互可靠性
zh.desc: 本文介绍了Omni-InteractScope，这是一个评估连续视听交互可靠性的基准。研究发现，当前的Omni-LLMs在及时工具使用、无查询提醒和持续指导方面存在显著不足。通过对1479个人工标注的交互进行评估，结果显示这些模型在工具调用的及时性和提醒的覆盖率上表现不佳。本文的发现强调了开发能够及时响应用户需求的流媒体助手的重要性。

papers.title: Cross-modal Steering Vectors Exist Across Both Image and Text Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract Cross-modal steering vectors transfer between text and image generation in unified multimodal models, revealing shared causal control mechanisms despite a modality gap.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Are concepts and mechanisms unified across modalities in current AI models, or instead implemented separately for each one? We operationalize this broad question of modality unification by studying cross-modal steering: 1) finding vectors that successfully steer generation on tokens of one modality, which then 2) transfer zero-shot to steer generation when added to tokens of another modality. Our study goes beyond simple correlational alignment (e.g. representational similarity) because steering is fundamentally causal. We study cross-modal steering in several unified multimodal models (UMMs), since they possess shared parameters for language and image generation, focusing on these two modalities. Across diverse steered concepts such as emotion and object size, we show that steering vectors transfer zero-shot in both directions (text-to-image & image-to-text). Even for concepts that are highly unique to one modality (e.g. formal vs. colloquial language), steering vectors often induce a consistent, interpretable effect in the other modality, such as formal clothing and design. This transfer has a geometric signature too: despite a clear modality gap separating text and image representations, steering vectors with strong cross-modal transferability tend to point in similar directions for the same concept. Our findings shed light on how vision and language interact inside unified multimodal models and point towards more general, modality-agnostic approaches for controlling their behavior.

ru.title: Общие причинно-следственные механизмы управления текстом и изображениями в одной модели
ru.desc: Авторы исследуют, объединены ли концепции между текстом и изображениями внутри унифицированных мультимодальных моделей (UMM) или реализованы отдельно для каждой модальности. Они используют cross-modal steering: вектор, найденный для управления генерацией одной модальности, добавляется к токенам другой модальности и переносится zero-shot без дополнительного обучения. Эксперименты показывают, что такие векторы работают в обоих направлениях (текст→изображение и изображение→текст), например, для эмоций и размера объектов. Геометрически сильные переносимые векторы направлены похоже, несмотря на заметный modality gap между представлениями текста и изображений.

en.title: Bridging Text and Image: Unifying Control in AI Models
en.desc: This paper explores how unified multimodal models (UMMs) can transfer control mechanisms between text and image generation. It introduces the concept of cross-modal steering vectors, which can influence generation in one modality based on learned representations from another. The study demonstrates that these vectors can effectively transfer zero-shot, meaning they can be applied without additional training, across text and image tasks. The findings suggest that there are shared causal relationships between modalities, indicating a deeper unification in how AI models understand and generate content across different forms of media.

zh.title: 跨模态引导：文本与图像的统一控制
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了跨模态引导向量在文本和图像生成中的应用，揭示了尽管存在模态差异，但它们之间共享的因果控制机制。研究表明，通过找到能够有效引导一种模态生成的向量，这些向量可以在零样本情况下转移到另一种模态的生成中。我们在多个统一的多模态模型中进行研究，发现引导向量在文本到图像和图像到文本之间都能实现零样本转移。研究结果表明，视觉和语言在统一的多模态模型中是如何相互作用的，并指向更通用的、与模态无关的控制方法。

papers.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Under KL-regularized control, a policy encodes its harness preferences, so deployed performance equals harness potential minus policy mismatch, and harness comparisons must separate these terms to predict training gains.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Language model agents are post-trained and deployed through a harness, the prompts, tools, and control logic that present a task to the model and execute its outputs. Harnesses are often revised and judged by how an already trained model performs under them, which assumes that what the model learned under one harness carries over to the next. We ask what a policy learns from its harness and what survives when the harness changes. Under KL-regularized control, we show that the log odds of an optimal policy recover how strongly its harness favors each action over the others, so a trained policy carries the preferences of its harness. Deployed return then equals the ceiling of the harness, the best return it offers, minus the mismatch of the policy, the return lost to its own suboptimal decisions. Training changes only the mismatch, while changing the harness moves both terms. Comparing harnesses with a fixed model therefore mixes what each harness offers with how well that model uses it. In MiniWoB++, post-training makes a model's preferences specific to its training harness. Reversing the order of the observation fields leaves every optimal decision unchanged yet lowers a trained model's success from 85.0% to 19.2%. Conversely, every new harness that a fixed-model comparison rejects but that raises the ceiling outperforms the original agent after further training under it, and ceiling and mismatch measured beforehand predict these gains. For coding-agent harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite, ceiling minus mismatch estimated with a stronger model as a stand-in for the optimum reproduces the accuracy ranking, while either term alone does not. Code is available at https://github.com/2020-qqtcg/HRP.
