The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Модель учится не только задаче, но и среде: сравнивайте harness отдельно от политики
ru.desc: Статья показывает, что при KL-регуляризованном управлении политика языковой модели (LLM) запоминает предпочтения своего harness, то есть набора промптов, инструментов и логики управления. Итоговая отдача равна потолку harness минус рассогласование политики, то есть потерям из-за её собственных неоптимальных решений. При дообучении меняется только рассогласование, а смена harness влияет на оба слагаемых. Поэтому сравнение harness при фиксированной модели смешивает качество самого harness и умение модели им пользоваться, и предварительно измеренные потолок и рассогласование позволяют предсказать выигрыш от дообучения.

en.title: Harnessing Learning: Understanding Policy Performance Through KL-Regularization
en.desc: This paper explores how machine learning policies learn from their harnesses, which are the frameworks used to train and deploy models. It introduces KL-regularized control to separate the performance potential of a harness from the policy's own decision-making errors. The authors demonstrate that a trained policy retains the preferences of its harness, affecting its performance when the harness changes. They also show that comparing different harnesses with a fixed model can obscure the true performance gains achievable through further training under a new harness.

zh.title: 策略偏好与控制环境的关系
zh.desc: 本文探讨了在KL正则化控制下，策略如何编码其偏好，并分析了部署性能与策略不匹配之间的关系。研究表明，训练后的模型在不同的控制环境中表现出不同的偏好，而这些偏好会影响模型的决策效果。通过比较不同的控制环境，作者揭示了如何评估模型在新环境中的表现，以及如何预测训练收益。最终，研究强调了在训练过程中，策略的不匹配是影响性能的关键因素。

papers.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Reasoning effort in generative models acts as a credence good where higher compute does not guarantee better instance-level results, and an escalation strategy from low effort improves cost-efficiency.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Generative models increasingly expose a reasoning effort setting that lets users scale inference-time compute, trading higher cost for potentially improved performance. Users must choose an effort level before knowing whether extra reasoning will help, and even a successful run does not reveal whether the effort purchased was necessary. Reasoning effort is therefore a credence good: buyers observe the outcome but cannot assess the marginal value of the computation they paid for. In this work, we measure the counterfactual effect of effort levels on both proprietary and open-weight models on four benchmarks, spanning single-call reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks. Effort, it turns out, does not consistently preserve tasks that lower effort solves, can overspend, and can change trajectory behavior. First, we find that although higher effort can raise accuracy in aggregate, it frequently fails on tasks that lower effort solved. Second, on the subset of easy tasks that every effort level solves, higher effort is generally more costly, with the highest effort level costing up to 42x as much as the lowest. Lastly, effort changes not only how many tokens are used, but also how agents solve tasks: at higher effort, agents verify their own work more heavily and more often search for solutions than work through problems directly, both of which lengthen trajectories without necessarily altering the outcome. These findings show that naively choosing the highest level is not only cost-inefficient but also offers no guarantee of the best instance-level performance. A simple alternative, starting at the lowest effort and escalating only after a verified failure, matches or improves on fixed top effort across all models and benchmarks at lower cost for most proprietary models.

ru.title: Больше вычислений не значит лучше: начинайте с малого и эскалируйте только при ошибке
ru.desc: Статья исследует параметр reasoning effort в генеративных моделях, который позволяет масштабировать inference-time compute ценой роста стоимости. Авторы показывают, что более высокий effort не гарантирует лучший результат на уровне отдельных задач: модель может провалить задачи, которые решались при низком effort, и переплачивает за простые примеры до 42 раз. Также высокий effort меняет поведение агентов, заставляя их чаще проверять себя и искать решения, что удлиняет траектории без улучшения результата. Предложенная стратегия эскалации, начиная с минимального effort и повышая его только после подтвержденной ошибки, сопоставима или лучше фиксированного максимального effort и дешевле для большинства проприетарных LLM.

en.title: Optimize Reasoning Effort for Cost-Effective Performance
en.desc: This paper discusses how the reasoning effort in generative models can be viewed as a credence good, meaning that users cannot easily assess the value of the extra computation they pay for. It highlights that while increasing effort can improve overall accuracy, it often fails on tasks that lower effort can solve. The authors demonstrate that higher effort levels can lead to significantly higher costs without guaranteeing better performance, and they observe changes in how agents approach problem-solving at different effort levels. The study suggests a more efficient strategy of starting with low effort and only increasing it when necessary, which can yield better results at a lower cost.

zh.title: 推理努力：从最低开始，逐步提升
zh.desc: 在生成模型中，推理努力被视为一种信任商品，增加计算量并不一定能保证更好的结果。用户在不知道额外推理是否有帮助之前，必须选择一个努力水平，而即使成功运行也无法判断所花费的努力是否必要。研究发现，尽管更高的努力水平可以提高整体准确性，但在某些任务上却可能失败。此外，简单的策略是从最低努力开始，只有在验证失败后再增加努力，这样可以在大多数模型中以更低的成本获得相似或更好的性能。

papers.title: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Abstract The study introduces a benchmark and metric to evaluate whether robot navigation policies adapt continuous motion to obstacle safety semantics, revealing a gap in translating semantic caution into safe movement.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Safe household navigation requires robots to regulate clearance and speed according to what an obstacle is and how close it is, without unnecessary conservatism. Yet existing evaluations do not test whether semantic safety distinctions are reflected in continuous motion. To that end, we introduce OSMA-Bench, an Obstacle-Conditioned Safe Motion Adaptation Benchmark built on spatially matched scenario sets that differ only in obstacle type. We also propose the Semantic Sensitivity Index (SSI), which measures whether clearance and distance-dependent speed and smoothness follow the caution ordering of obstacles. Evaluating VLM-based and vision-language-action (VLA) policies on the benchmark, we find that neither consistently adapts its motion to obstacle safety, even with explicit safety prompts. Our analysis shows that the policies can correctly distinguish obstacles by safety relevance but fail to reflect this distinction in the motion parameters or actions they produce. For VLM-based policies, which recognize the obstacle and then generate a navigation program, adding an explicit parameter-inference step between these two stages improves adaptation. These findings expose a gap in semantic-to-motion grounding, highlighting the need to translate semantic caution into appropriately safe motion.

ru.title: От семантической осторожности к безопасному движению робота
ru.desc: В статье представлен бенчмарк OSMA-Bench и метрика Semantic Sensitivity Index (SSI) для оценки того, адаптируют ли навигационные политики робота непрерывное движение к семантике безопасности препятствий. Тестирование VLM-based и VLA-политик показало, что ни одна из них стабильно не меняет клиренс, скорость и плавность движения в зависимости от типа препятствия, даже при явных промптах о безопасности. Модели корректно различают препятствия по степени опасности, но не переносят это различие в параметры движения и действия. Добавление явного шага вывода параметров между распознаванием препятствия и генерацией навигационной программы улучшает адаптацию, что указывает на разрыв между семантикой и моторным управлением.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: From Semantic Safety to Safe Robot Motion
en.desc: This paper presents a new benchmark called OSMA-Bench to evaluate how well robot navigation policies adapt their movements based on the safety of obstacles. It identifies a significant issue where robots can recognize different obstacles but do not adjust their speed and clearance appropriately according to the level of caution required. The study introduces the Semantic Sensitivity Index (SSI) to measure how well these policies translate semantic safety into actual motion parameters. The findings indicate that existing models struggle to connect semantic understanding with safe navigation actions, suggesting a need for improved methods to bridge this gap.

zh.title: 将语义安全转化为安全运动的必要性
zh.desc: 本研究提出了一种基准和指标，用于评估机器人导航策略是否能够将连续运动适应于障碍物的安全语义。研究发现，现有评估方法未能测试语义安全的区别是否反映在连续运动中。我们引入了OSMA-Bench，这是一个基于障碍物类型的安全运动适应基准，并提出了语义敏感性指数（SSI），用于衡量运动参数是否遵循障碍物的安全等级。通过对基准的评估，我们发现现有的视觉语言模型（VLM）和视觉-语言-行动（VLA）策略未能有效地将运动适应于障碍物的安全性。

papers.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
papers.abstract: Abstract Prox replaces calibrated thresholds with top-k channel selection and a weight-derived reader to accelerate Mixture-of-Experts inference while preserving accuracy.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. Because most intermediate channels in a routed expert contribute little to any single token, channel selectors predict which channels matter and read only their weights, typically keeping channels above a threshold calibrated on offline data. We show that channel selection needs no calibration data. First, a calibrated threshold does not fix how much a selector reads, because the number of channels passing it varies across inputs; Prox with thresholds calibrated for an 18% read budget actually reads only 12.9% on average across our benchmarks. Second, top-k keeps each token's k highest-scoring channels and needs no calibration data. At the calibrated budget, a selector's top-k version matches or beats its threshold version on the same score in 40 of 43 comparisons at 13% and 18% budgets, including all 23 on generation tasks. The top-k versions also avoid the repetition-loop collapse that calibrated thresholds cause on Gemma 4. Calibrating a threshold thus provides neither of the two things selectors use it for: a known read budget and a consistent accuracy gain at that budget. We furthermore introduce a reader built entirely from the model's weights, which screens channels with a ternary sketch and recovers the skipped ones with a low-rank map. Across three post-trained MoE models, our reader retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads, with Triton kernels running MoE blocks 1.60 to 1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one and up to 2.69x at larger batches on the same three models.

ru.title: Быстрее MoE без калибровки: читай только нужные каналы
ru.desc: В статье предлагается ускорить инференс Mixture-of-Experts моделей, где узким местом является загрузка весов маршрутизируемых экспертов из памяти при небольших батчах. Авторы показывают, что калибровка порога для выбора каналов не нужна: метод top-k, выбирающий k наиболее значимых каналов для каждого токена, не требует калибровочных данных и стабильно не хуже порогового подхода. Также вводится reader, построенный только по весам модели: он отбирает каналы с помощью тернарного sketch и восстанавливает пропущенные через low-rank отображение. Метод сохраняет 98.1% точности полной модели, читая лишь 17.8% весов экспертов, и ускоряет MoE-блоки в 1.6–2.69 раза по сравнению с оптимизированным vLLM.

en.title: Accelerating Mixture-of-Experts with Top-k Channel Selection
en.desc: This paper introduces Prox, a method that enhances the efficiency of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by replacing traditional calibrated thresholds with a top-k channel selection strategy. The authors demonstrate that using top-k selection eliminates the need for calibration data while maintaining or improving accuracy during inference. They reveal that calibrated thresholds do not consistently control the amount of data read, leading to inefficiencies, whereas top-k selection ensures that only the most relevant channels are accessed. Additionally, a novel reader mechanism is proposed, which utilizes the model's weights to optimize channel screening and retrieval, resulting in significant speed improvements without sacrificing accuracy.

zh.title: Prox：加速混合专家推理的新方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为Prox的方法，通过选择top-k通道和基于权重的读取器来加速混合专家模型的推理，同时保持准确性。传统的阈值校准方法在小批量解码时会导致性能瓶颈，而Prox通过预测重要通道并仅读取其权重，避免了这种问题。研究表明，top-k选择不需要校准数据，并且在多个基准测试中表现优于传统的阈值方法。最终，Prox方法在保持高准确率的同时，显著提高了模型的运行速度。

papers.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
papers.abstract: Abstract LongChang evaluates whether LLMs can autonomously discover altered physical laws through simulated experimentation, finding that only one model achieved limited success.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

ru.title: Может ли AI переоткрыть законы физики сам?
ru.desc: Статья представляет LongChang — автоматический фреймворк, который создаёт симулированные миры с изменёнными законами физики, где LLM выступают в роли исследователей. Модели самостоятельно манипулируют объектами, строят инструменты и формулируют гипотезы без подсказок о том, какие законы искать. Отдельные LLM-агенты генерируют сцены, проверяют инструменты и оценивают отчёты, а результаты экспериментов направляют эволюцию сцен, и весь цикл работает без участия человека. Из 12 протестированных моделей лишь GPT-6-Astra открыла законы в 16,7% случаев, остальные не справились, а логи экспериментов показывают лишь частичное выявление изменённой физики.

en.title: Exploring New Physics: LLMs as Autonomous Discoverers
en.desc: The paper investigates the ability of large language models (LLMs) to autonomously discover new physical laws in simulated environments with altered physics. Using a framework called LongChang, the researchers created scenarios where traditional physics does not apply, allowing LLMs to explore and experiment without explicit guidance. Among the tested models, only GPT-6-Astra demonstrated a limited success rate of 16.7% in identifying these new laws, while the others failed to make any discoveries. The findings highlight the challenges LLMs face in recognizing and investigating anomalies in unfamiliar physical contexts.

zh.title: 探索未知：LLMs能否发现改变的物理定律？
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）是否能够通过模拟实验自主发现改变的物理定律。研究使用了一个名为LongChang的自动化框架，创建了具有不同物理规律的模拟世界。评估的LLMs作为探索者，操控物体并构建工具，自主提出问题，而无需研究任务或提示。结果显示，只有GPT-6-Astra模型在发现率上取得了16.7%的成功，其余11个模型均未能发现任何新规律。

papers.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract VibeVideoBench evaluates multimodal agents that generate videos via code, finding that top systems meet core requirements on most tasks but frequently fail due to poor time management.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. We introduce VibeVideoBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on code-driven video generation. Its 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese span 12 categories, from data stories and music-driven pieces to classroom lessons and paper explainers; each asks an agent, running in its native harness inside a sandbox with no image or video generation model, to deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour. Evaluation is hierarchical and evidence-based: program checks of the delivery spec, about 13k task-specific rubric checks traced to the requirements they enforce, and five quality dimensions anchored per task, scored by three VLM judge panels. Across nine frontier agent systems and 2,151 scored rollouts, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 rank first and second with both the judges and human annotators, and the strongest system satisfies every core requirement on 76.3% of tasks. Delivery is a second axis: counting missing videos as zero changes the ranking, and three quarters of the lost videos are final renders that started too late, ran too slowly or never started, a failure of how agents plan their hour. Agents build their own rendering pipelines and inspect their own frames, yet how much they look does not predict quality. The judges' ranking of the systems closely matches blind human preferences.

ru.title: Агенты умеют писать видео по коду, но часто не успевают вовремя
ru.desc: В статье представлен VibeVideoBench — бенчмарк для оценки мультимодальных LLM-агентов, которые создают видео через написание кода, а не с помощью diffusion-моделей. Набор включает 239 задач на английском и китайском языках в 12 категориях и требует от агента выдать готовый MP4 со звуком за один час в изолированной песочнице. Оценка иерархическая: программные проверки, около 13 тысяч рубрик и три панели VLM-судей по пяти измерениям качества, сверенные с предпочтениями людей. Главный вывод: лучшие системы выполняют основные требования в 76,3% задач, но многие видео теряются из-за плохого тайм-менеджмента, а не из-за качества кода.

en.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Code-Driven Video Generation Agents
en.desc: The paper introduces VibeVideoBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal agents that generate videos through code. It highlights that while leading systems can meet many requirements, they often struggle with time management, leading to incomplete or poorly synchronized outputs. The benchmark consists of 239 tasks across various categories, requiring agents to produce videos within a strict time limit without relying on pre-existing video generation models. Evaluation is thorough, involving program checks and quality assessments by multiple judge panels, revealing that the top-performing agents excel in meeting core requirements but face challenges in timely delivery.

zh.title: VibeVideoBench：智能体视频生成的新标准
zh.desc: VibeVideoBench 是一个评估多模态智能体生成视频的基准。研究发现，尽管顶尖系统在大多数任务上满足核心要求，但由于时间管理不善，常常失败。该基准包含239个自包含的任务，涵盖12个类别，要求智能体在一小时内生成带声音的完整视频。评估采用分层和基于证据的方法，确保了生成内容的质量和准确性。

papers.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Just Action Model decouples backbone initialization, future observation objectives, and inference machinery to improve robot control with foresight training and reduced computation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) communities debate whether control policies should inherit pretrained knowledge from vision-language models or from visual generators. The debate, however, bundles three separable choices: backbone initialization, the objective applied to future observations, and whether the machinery for that future loss is kept at inference. A gap between a VLA and a WAM therefore cannot simply be attributed to any one of them. We show that decoupling these choices yields a common framework for both families, which we term Just Action Model (JAM): a pretrained visual backbone with an action expert, trained with an action loss and a foresight loss. The foresight loss trains current-observation features to predict frozen encodings of the recorded future through a prediction head discarded after training, so no visual generation is involved in either training or inference, and the backbone can be chosen freely. We first compare objectives within fixed policy architectures, then evaluate the foresight recipe across backbone families. The resulting JAM policies outperform their matched FastWAM and ImageWAM counterparts on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and achieve similar or slightly higher success rates on RoboTwin. Compared with FastWAM, JAM improves the success rates from 97.0%/55.3%/91.2% to 98.2%/64.5%/91.4%, respectively. With cached foresight targets, JAM reduces estimated online training FLOPs per sample per update by 73% relative to FastWAM. Our results show that future supervision improves control without visual generation or additional inference machinery, and strong foresight performance is attainable with either generator-initialized or vision-language backbones. Project Page: https://y0uroy.github.io/JAM

ru.title: Предвидеть будущее без генерации: прогноз ради управления
ru.desc: Авторы разбирают спор между VLA и WAM моделями управления роботами и показывают, что он смешивает три независимых решения: инициализацию backbone, цель для будущих наблюдений и наличие механизма future loss на инференсе. Предложенная модель JAM использует предобученный визуальный backbone с action expert и обучается по двум функциям потерь: action loss и foresight loss. Foresight loss заставляет признаки текущего наблюдения предсказывать замороженные эмбеддинги будущего через prediction head, который отбрасывается после обучения, поэтому визуальная генерация не нужна ни при обучении, ни при инференсе. JAM превосходит аналогичные FastWAM и ImageWAM на LIBERO и LIBERO-Plus и сокращает вычисления на обучение примерно на 73%.

en.title: Decoupling for Superior Robot Control with JAM
en.desc: The Just Action Model (JAM) introduces a new approach to robot control by separating key components such as backbone initialization and future observation objectives. This model utilizes a pretrained visual backbone combined with an action expert, focusing on training with foresight loss to enhance prediction capabilities. By decoupling these elements, JAM provides a unified framework that outperforms existing models like FastWAM and ImageWAM in various tasks. Additionally, JAM significantly reduces computational costs during training, demonstrating that effective control can be achieved without relying on visual generation during inference.

zh.title: 解耦未来观察，提升机器人控制
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为Just Action Model（JAM）的新模型，旨在通过解耦骨干初始化、未来观察目标和推理机制来改善机器人控制。JAM使用预训练的视觉骨干和动作专家，通过动作损失和前瞻损失进行训练，从而提高控制性能。研究表明，未来监督可以在不涉及视觉生成或额外推理机制的情况下改善控制效果。实验结果显示，JAM在多个基准测试中超越了现有的控制策略，且在线训练的计算量显著减少。

papers.title: OvisOCR3 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Abstract OvisOCR3 is a compact 0.8B vision-language model that unifies diverse OCR tasks through multi-teacher distillation and reinforcement learning, achieving state-of-the-art results across document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction, figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce OvisOCR3, a 0.8B model for a broad range of OCR-related tasks. OvisOCR3 unifies document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction (KIE), document figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction in a single model. We train the model on real and synthetic data through continued pretraining and use domain-balanced mid-training to balance supervision across tasks with different data volumes and response lengths. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation transfers expertise from five domain-specific 4B teachers into the shared model, followed by mixed-task reinforcement learning with domain-specific rewards. We compare OvisOCR3 with general-purpose vision-language models and specialized OCR models on public and in-house benchmarks covering all five task families. In these comparisons, it achieves an overall score of 96.74 on OmniDocBench v1.6 and the highest overall scores on PureDocBench, Real5-OmniDocBench, and MDPBench. On OCRBench v2, it ranks first, scoring 65.9 and 61.3 on the English and Chinese splits, respectively. It also outperforms the baselines on OCRBench and all four KIE benchmarks. On DocFigCapBench, it achieves the highest localization F1 and a caption score close to that of Qwen3.8-Max. For cross-page tables, it leads in Relation F1 on CrossTabBench and truncated-table TEDS on MPDocBench-Parse. These results demonstrate that a compact 0.8B model can achieve strong performance across diverse OCR-related tasks. OvisOCR3 is available at https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/OvisOCR3.

ru.title: Компактная модель 0,8B — универсальный мастер OCR
ru.desc: В статье представлена OvisOCR3 — компактная vision-language модель с 0,8 млрд параметров, которая объединяет несколько OCR-задач: разбор документов, общее OCR, извлечение ключевой информации (KIE), подписи к рисункам и реконструкцию таблиц, разбитых между страницами. Модель обучается на реальных и синтетических данных с использованием continued pretraining и сбалансированного mid-training, а знания переносятся от пяти доменных учителей по 4 млрд параметров через multi-teacher on-policy distillation. Финальный этап — mixed-task reinforcement learning с доменно-специфичными наградами. По результатам бенчмарков модель достигает state-of-the-art качества на ряде задач, демонстрируя, что небольшая модель может конкурировать с гораздо более крупными.

en.title: Unifying OCR Tasks with a Compact Vision-Language Model
en.desc: OvisOCR3 is a compact vision-language model designed for various Optical Character Recognition (OCR) tasks, achieving impressive results with only 0.8 billion parameters. It integrates multiple tasks such as document parsing, key information extraction, and figure captioning into a single framework through advanced training techniques like multi-teacher distillation and reinforcement learning. The model is trained on both real and synthetic datasets, ensuring balanced performance across tasks with different data characteristics. Its state-of-the-art performance is validated through rigorous benchmarking against both general-purpose and specialized OCR models, showcasing its versatility and efficiency in handling diverse OCR challenges.

zh.title: OvisOCR3：小型模型的大能力
zh.desc: OvisOCR3是一个紧凑的0.8B视觉语言模型，能够统一多种OCR任务。它通过多教师蒸馏和强化学习的方法，提升了文档解析、一般OCR、关键信息提取、图表说明和跨页表格重建等任务的性能。该模型在真实和合成数据上进行训练，并通过领域平衡的中期训练来平衡不同任务的数据量和响应长度。OvisOCR3在多个基准测试中表现优异，展示了小型模型在多样化OCR任务中的强大能力。

papers.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
papers.abstract: Abstract RynnWorld-Latent learns cross-embodiment world dynamics via 3D-grounded latent actions, enabling joint pretraining on diverse video sources and synthetic data generation for improved robot policy performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Learning controllable world dynamics from heterogeneous interaction videos is challenging because robot embodiments use incompatible action spaces, while human videos lack native control labels. We present RynnWorld-Latent, a cross-embodiment video world model that uses the 3D-grounded latent actions introduced by RynnLAM as a shared conditioning interface. This representation enables joint pretraining on human interaction videos, robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without requiring a common native action space. Built on a pretrained video transformer, RynnWorld-Latent combines global action tokens with an identity-initialized local pathway that aligns actions with future video latents. We pretrain on 23 datasets comprising approximately 553.5M frames and adapt the model to target robots through post-training. The framework supports two data-generation routes: digital teleoperation uses target robot commands to generate action-video demonstrations, while latent-action synthesis transfers source motion to an edited initial frame and pairs the resulting rollout with retargeted pseudo robot actions. Experiments show improved video prediction metrics on public benchmarks and two real-robot platforms, alongside qualitative action following when different action sequences share the same initial observation. Synthetic mid-training improves policy success rates on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and both generation routes improve real-world policy success rates over real-demonstration-only training in the evaluated settings. These results support universal latent actions as a scalable interface for learning controllable visual dynamics across heterogeneous embodiments.

ru.title: Универсальные латентные действия — единый язык управления роботами
ru.desc: В статье представлена RynnWorld-Latent — кросс-эмбодимент модель мира на основе видео, которая использует 3D-grounded латентные действия (RynnLAM) как общий интерфейс управления. Такой подход позволяет совместно предобучать модель на видео с участием людей, демонстрациях роботов и симуляциях без единого нативного пространства действий. Модель построена на предобученном video transformer и обучена на 23 датасетах (около 553,5M кадров), после чего адаптируется к целевым роботам через post-training. Эксперименты показывают улучшение метрик предсказания видео и успешности политик робота на LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus и двух реальных платформах, а синтетические данные повышают качество обучения.

en.title: Learning Universal Actions for Diverse Robot Dynamics
en.desc: The paper introduces RynnWorld-Latent, a model that learns to understand and predict world dynamics across different robot embodiments using 3D-grounded latent actions. This approach allows the model to be pretrained on a variety of video sources, including human interactions and robot demonstrations, without needing a common action space. By leveraging a pretrained video transformer, the model aligns actions with future video frames, enhancing its ability to generate synthetic data for training. The results demonstrate improved performance in video prediction and real-world robot policy success rates, showcasing the effectiveness of universal latent actions for diverse robotic applications.

zh.title: 跨体现学习可控视觉动态的创新模型
zh.desc: RynnWorld-Latent 是一种跨体现世界模型，通过3D基础的潜在动作学习世界动态，能够在多样的视频源和合成数据生成上进行联合预训练，从而提升机器人策略的表现。该模型解决了机器人和人类视频之间不兼容的动作空间问题，利用共享的条件接口进行训练。通过在23个数据集上进行预训练，RynnWorld-Latent 结合了全局动作标记和局部路径，以对齐未来视频的潜在动作。实验结果表明，该框架在视频预测和真实机器人平台上均表现出色，支持在不同体现间学习可控的视觉动态。

papers.title: SearchHorizonBench: A Benchmark for Search Value in AI Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract SearchHorizonBench evaluates how agents learn to estimate the value of additional search from execution history, showing that historical calibration improves prediction accuracy but leaves most search-gain variance unexplained.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small AI agents must decide when another search is worth its cost. Answer-success probabilities capture question difficulty, while this decision requires estimating the additional benefit of search. We introduce SearchHorizonBench, a benchmark for learning and evaluating search value from execution experience. Paired continuations and repeated executions separate expected search gain from generation noise and connect prediction quality to decision utility. The resource contains 45,632 executions across 3,168 questions. On 1,632 held-out questions, historical calibration reduces Brier error by 16.2%, with the improvement concentrated in success-level information. Search gains have a standard deviation of 21.4 percentage points, and tested historical estimators explain less than 2% of this variance in point estimates. Matched-configuration learning curves probe this distinction across training scales. At the reference token price, free selection observations yield a 2.49-point utility opportunity over the best constant action, driven primarily by gain information. Reusable histories, frozen splits, strong baselines and scoring tools provide a common foundation for developing and evaluating value-aware search agents.

ru.title: Знать, когда искать: оценка ценности дополнительного поиска для AI-агентов
ru.desc: Статья представляет SearchHorizonBench — бенчмарк для обучения и оценки того, насколько полезен дополнительный поиск для AI-агентов, основанный на истории выполнения. Авторы разделяют ожидаемый прирост от поиска и шум генерации с помощью парных продолжений и повторных запусков. Исторская калибровка снижает ошибку Brier на 16.2%, но исторические оценщики объясняют менее 2% дисперсии прироста поиска. Ресурс содержит 45 632 выполнения по 3 168 вопросам и предоставляет инструменты для разработки value-aware поисковых агентов.

en.title: Enhancing Search Value Estimation with Historical Calibration
en.desc: The paper introduces SearchHorizonBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate how agents learn to estimate the value of additional search based on their execution history. It demonstrates that while historical calibration can improve prediction accuracy, it does not account for most of the variance in search gains. The study includes a large dataset of 45,632 executions across various questions, revealing that historical estimators explain less than 2% of the variance in search gain predictions. Ultimately, the research highlights the importance of understanding the utility of search decisions and provides tools for developing more effective value-aware search agents.

zh.title: 提升搜索价值的智能体评估基准
zh.desc: 本文介绍了SearchHorizonBench，这是一个用于评估智能体如何从执行历史中学习搜索价值的基准。研究表明，历史校准可以提高预测准确性，但仍然无法解释大部分搜索增益的方差。智能体需要判断额外搜索是否值得其成本，而成功概率则反映了问题的难度。通过配对延续和重复执行，本文将预期搜索增益与生成噪声分开，从而将预测质量与决策效用联系起来。

papers.title: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract HaMo combines rapid retrieval of procedural experience cards with gradual model adaptation to improve long-horizon web agents' retention and cross-task execution.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-horizon agents continuously encounter reusable procedural knowledge, yet existing systems typically rely either on model adaptation or external memory, trading persistent learning for rapid reuse. This limitation is especially important for Web agents that repeatedly execute related multi-step workflows. We propose HaMo, a Harness-Model collaborative framework that combines fast non-parametric experience accumulation with slow parametric adaptation. HaMo distills trajectories into strategy-level experience cards for immediate retrieval, while an experience-conditioned continual learning objective trains the model to interpret, ground, and execute retrieved strategies across changing contexts. A retrieval-coverage-based selection mechanism further identifies compact and complementary trajectories for parameter updates. Experiments show that HaMo outperforms harness-only and model-only adaptation under within-domain and cross-domain shifts, improving both retention and adaptation. These results highlight the importance of jointly preserving procedural experience and internalizing the competence to transfer and execute it across tasks.

ru.title: Память плюс обучение: агент, который не забывает и умеет переносить опыт
ru.desc: Статья представляет HaMo — фреймворк, в котором LLM-агент для работы с веб-интерфейсами совмещает два подхода: быстрое непараметрическое накопление опыта в виде карточек стратегий и медленную параметрическую адаптацию самой модели. Траектории выполнения задач сжимаются в карточки опыта, которые извлекаются из внешней памяти и подаются модели, а continual learning-цель обучает модель интерпретировать и выполнять эти стратегии в меняющихся контекстах. Механизм отбора на основе покрытия при извлечении выбирает компактные и взаимодополняющие траектории для обновления параметров. Эксперименты показывают, что HaMo превосходит как подход только с памятью, так и подход только с дообучением модели, как внутри домена, так и при переносе на другие домены.

en.title: Enhancing Web Agents with Fast Retrieval and Gradual Learning
en.desc: HaMo is a framework designed to enhance the performance of long-horizon web agents by combining quick access to procedural knowledge with gradual model learning. It uses experience cards that summarize strategies for immediate use, allowing agents to efficiently execute multi-step tasks. The framework balances fast retrieval of past experiences with slow updates to the model, ensuring that agents can adapt to new contexts while retaining useful information. Experiments demonstrate that HaMo significantly improves both the retention of knowledge and the ability to adapt to different tasks compared to traditional methods.

zh.title: HaMo：提升网络代理的知识保留与跨任务执行能力
zh.desc: HaMo是一种结合快速检索程序经验卡和逐步模型适应的方法，旨在提高长时间跨度网络代理的知识保留和跨任务执行能力。该框架通过快速的非参数经验积累与缓慢的参数适应相结合，解决了现有系统在快速重用和持久学习之间的权衡问题。HaMo能够将轨迹提炼为策略级经验卡，以便于即时检索，同时通过经验条件的持续学习目标训练模型，使其能够在变化的上下文中理解、落实和执行检索到的策略。实验结果表明，HaMo在领域内和跨领域的任务转移中均优于仅依赖于经验或模型的适应方法，显著提高了知识的保留和适应能力。

papers.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Abstract NLD-Uni is a unified discrete diffusion language model that combines visual understanding and generation via cross-paradigm on-policy distillation and progressive self-refining diffusion.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We propose Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni (NLD-Uni), a unified discrete diffusion large language model (DLLM) for visual understanding and generation tasks. Compared with prior unified diffusion models, NLD-Uni introduces two major innovations. First, we propose a unified cross-paradigm on-policy distillation (OPD) framework that successfully transfers the visual understanding ability of autoregressive VLMs and visual generation ability of continuous flow models, to a unified DLLM. Second, NLD-Uni incorporates a novel progressive self-refining diffusion process that gradually corrupts each token across multiple steps during training, as opposed to adopting the conventional masked diffusion formulation that directly corrupts a clean image token to an uninformative mask token. At inference, this design allows NLD-Uni to make intermediate commit to a token, enabling progressive self-refinement for better visual quality. Through extensive experiments, we show that NLD-Uni achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified DLLMs on diverse tasks including visual question-answering, multi-modal reasoning, object grounding, text-to-image generation, and image editing.

ru.title: Одна дискретная диффузионная модель для понимания и создания изображений
ru.desc: В статье представлена NLD-Uni — унифицированная языковая модель с дискретной диффузией (DLLM), которая одновременно понимает и генерирует изображения. Авторы переносят знания от авторегрессионных VLM и моделей непрерывных потоков (flow models) с помощью кросс-парадигменной on-policy дистилляции (OPD). Ключевая новизна — прогрессивный самоуточняющий процесс диффузии, где токены постепенно искажаются за несколько шагов, а не сразу заменяются маской, что позволяет промежуточно фиксировать токены и улучшать качество изображения. Модель достигает state-of-the-art результатов среди унифицированных DLLM в задачах visual question answering, мультимодального рассуждения, grounding, text-to-image генерации и редактирования изображений.

en.title: Revolutionizing Visual Understanding with NLD-Uni
en.desc: NLD-Uni is a novel discrete diffusion language model that integrates visual understanding and generation through innovative techniques. It introduces a unified cross-paradigm on-policy distillation framework that effectively merges the strengths of autoregressive visual language models and continuous flow models. Additionally, NLD-Uni employs a progressive self-refining diffusion process that enhances token corruption during training, allowing for improved visual quality during inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that NLD-Uni outperforms existing models in various tasks such as visual question-answering and text-to-image generation.

zh.title: 统一视觉理解与生成的创新模型
zh.desc: NLD-Uni是一种统一的离散扩散语言模型，旨在通过跨范式的在线蒸馏和渐进自我精炼扩散来结合视觉理解和生成。与之前的统一扩散模型相比，NLD-Uni引入了两个主要创新：首先，提出了一种统一的跨范式在线蒸馏框架，成功地将自回归视觉语言模型的视觉理解能力和连续流模型的视觉生成能力转移到统一的离散扩散大语言模型中。其次，NLD-Uni采用了一种新颖的渐进自我精炼扩散过程，在训练过程中逐步破坏每个标记，而不是直接将干净的图像标记破坏为无信息的掩码标记。这种设计使得NLD-Uni在推理时能够对标记进行中间承诺，从而实现渐进自我精炼，提高视觉质量。

papers.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract SPOT accelerates diffusion language models by predicting token generation order and verifying candidates in parallel, reducing passes up to 6.8x while maintaining exact decoding.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at over 90% of positions, but not which position comes next. We introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), a 0.62M-parameter model that reads only the target's output distributions, predicts this order and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, which the target verifies in a single pass by state equality. Coupled-noise match, which shares Gumbel noise between drafter and target, keeps this verification exact at any temperature. This approach also inspired us to introduce SPOT-Sets for dynamic threshold decoding, where a pass commits several positions: SPOT-Sets drafts whole commit sets together with their tokens. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8times and reaches up to 3.4times the throughput of standard decoding on SDAR-8B, matching or beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at T=0 and T=1. In addition, we show that SPOT's learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs; with a light calibration, the SPOT-Sets drafter transfers as well. On top of dynamic threshold decoding, SPOT-Sets improves the throughput of SDAR-8B by 59% on average over the threshold decoder alone. Project page: https://eliezer318.github.io/SPOT-dLLM/

ru.title: Предсказываем порядок — генерируем текст в разы быстрее без потери качества
ru.desc: Диффузионные языковые модели (DLM) умеют генерировать текст параллельно, но обычно приходится выбирать между скоростью и качеством. Авторы предлагают SPOT, небольшую модель с 0.62M параметров, которая предсказывает порядок заполнения позиций и строит дерево кандидатов, проверяемых основной моделью за один проход без потери качества. Метод сохраняет точность декодирования при любой температуре благодаря совместному шуму Гамбеля для драфтера и целевой модели. Вариант SPOT-Sets позволяет фиксировать сразу несколько позиций за проход при динамическом пороговом декодировании и переносится между разными DLM, сокращая число проходов до 6.8 раза.

en.title: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models with SPOT
en.desc: The paper introduces SPOT, a method that enhances the efficiency of diffusion language models (DLMs) by predicting the order of token generation and verifying multiple candidates simultaneously. This approach significantly reduces the number of passes required for decoding, achieving up to 6.8 times faster performance while ensuring exact decoding. SPOT leverages the model's own predictions to determine the next token positions, allowing for a more streamlined generation process. Additionally, SPOT-Sets is introduced for dynamic threshold decoding, further improving throughput and demonstrating effective transferability across different DLMs.

zh.title: SPOT：加速扩散语言模型的创新方法
zh.desc: SPOT是一种加速扩散语言模型的方法，通过预测生成顺序并并行验证候选项，减少了多达6.8倍的模型传递，同时保持精确解码。传统的精确解码每次只填补一个掩码位置，而快速的多标记解码方案则会损失信息。SPOT通过预测生成顺序，利用模型在前一次传递中的预测，确保在90%以上的位置上生成正确的标记。我们的实验表明，SPOT在多个任务中都能显著提高生成速度，并且在不同的扩散语言模型之间成功迁移。

papers.title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
papers.abstract: Abstract A world model predicts machine learning program outcomes to enable affordable test-time scaling for AI research agents, improving performance with fewer real executions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small AI research agents can propose, execute, and improve programs that solve machine learning tasks. However, executing each candidate program requires training and evaluating ML models, limiting how many candidates an agent can explore at each step. We introduce MLE-World, a world model finetuned from Qwen3.5-4B that predicts a program's terminal output (error traces, training logs, and validation scores) from its code and data description without executing it, together with a confidence score estimating the prediction's correctness. Because a prediction costs one inference call rather than a training run, MLE-World makes test time scaling (TTS) affordable for these agents. We build five TTS policies, guided by MLE-World, that compare several candidates per step by their predicted outputs: Sequential revision, Best-of-N, Pairwise judging, Fusion, and a UCB style rule that also adds an exploration bonus from this confidence score. Since predictions can be wrong, we run a candidate for real only when its confidence score is low. On 17 MLE-bench Lite tasks, MLE-World matches the real terminal output on 77.9% of held out programs, versus 41.1% for much larger prompted models. MLE-World guided TTS achieves up to 22.1% higher observed mean performance than the agent without a world model, with less real execution. Project webpage: https://mle-world.github.io/.

ru.title: Предсказывай результат ML-программы, не запуская её
ru.desc: Статья представляет MLE-World — world model на основе Qwen3.5-4B, которая предсказывает результат выполнения ML-программы (логи ошибок, данные обучения и валидационные метрики) по коду и описанию данных, не запуская её. Модель также выдаёт confidence score, оценивающий надёжность предсказания. Благодаря тому, что предсказание требует лишь одного вызова LLM вместо обучения модели, test-time scaling становится дешёвым для AI-агентов, которые исследуют кандидатов на решение задач машинного обучения. На 17 задачах MLE-bench Lite MLE-World точно воспроизводит реальный результат в 77.9% случаев, а агент с её помощью достигает до 22.1% более высокой средней производительности при меньшем числе реальных запусков.

en.title: Predicting Success: MLE-World Enhances AI Program Testing Efficiency
en.desc: The paper introduces MLE-World, a world model that predicts the outcomes of machine learning programs without executing them, thus enabling more efficient exploration of candidate solutions. By using a finetuned model from Qwen3.5-4B, MLE-World can estimate a program's performance metrics and provide a confidence score for its predictions. This approach allows AI research agents to evaluate multiple candidates quickly, reducing the need for costly training runs. The results show that MLE-World significantly improves performance on various tasks while minimizing real execution time.

zh.title: 用MLE-World提升AI测试效率
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种名为MLE-World的世界模型，它可以预测机器学习程序的结果，从而降低AI研究代理在测试时的执行成本。通过不执行程序，MLE-World能够根据代码和数据描述预测程序的最终输出，并提供一个置信度评分来评估预测的正确性。这样，代理可以在每一步探索更多候选程序，而不必进行大量的训练和评估。实验结果表明，MLE-World在多个任务中显著提高了性能，减少了实际执行的需求。

papers.title: Timestral
papers.abstract: Abstract Timestral is a family of time series foundation models that achieves state-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting through decoupled horizon forecasting, native future covariate support, and synthetic pretraining followed by mixed post-training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric. We achieve this with three ingredients: Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), which separates prediction tokens from the causally encoded context, so that longer horizons are trained without masking context and each observed value is both a forecast target and context for later forecasts; a covariate framework that natively supports known-future covariates within a causal architecture; and a two-stage pipeline that pretrains exclusively on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus before post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data with extended context. This report describes the model design and its benchmark results. Weights for all four models are available on Hugging Face and inference code on GitHub.

ru.title: Новый стандарт вероятностного прогнозирования временных рядов, обученный на синтетике
ru.desc: В статье представлено семейство моделей-фундаментов для временных рядов Timestral, состоящее из четырёх моделей от 5M до 209M параметров. Ключевой метод — Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), который отделяет токены предсказания от каузально закодированного контекста, позволяя обучать длинные горизонты без маскирования контекста. Модели поддерживают известные будущие ковариаты внутри каузальной архитектуры и обучаются в два этапа: предобучение только на большом синтетическом корпусе и дообучение на смеси реальных и синтетических данных с расширенным контекстом. Timestral устанавливает новый state of the art на бенчмарках GIFT-Eval, TIME и fev-bench, занимая два первых места по всем метрикам.

en.title: Revolutionizing Time Series Forecasting with Timestral
en.desc: Timestral is a new family of time series models designed for probabilistic forecasting, achieving top performance on various benchmarks. It utilizes Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF) to improve predictions by separating forecast targets from the context, allowing for better handling of longer time horizons. The models also incorporate a framework for known-future covariates, enhancing their predictive capabilities within a causal structure. With a two-stage training process that combines synthetic and real data, Timestral sets new standards in forecasting accuracy and efficiency.

zh.title: 时间序列预测的新标杆
zh.desc: Timestral是一系列时间序列基础模型，专注于概率预测，采用了分离的预测视角和原生的未来协变量支持。该模型通过合成预训练和混合后训练的方法，达到了最新的预测精度。Timestral在多个基准测试中表现优异，尤其是Timestral-209M和Timestral-123M在所有指标上均名列前茅。该模型设计结合了分离预测、协变量框架和两阶段训练流程，展示了其在时间序列预测中的强大能力。

papers.title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds
papers.abstract: Abstract Physevolve trains vision-language models in causal physical reasoning by using a physics engine to validate self-generated executable worlds and counterfactual simulations, improving performance on dynamics benchmarks without human data.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality. Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The self-evolving paradigm offers a route beyond fixed datasets by enabling models to construct their own training problems. Extending this paradigm to physics, however, requires an external source of truth that can both validate model-proposed environments and verify alternative physical outcomes under intervention. We introduce , a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation-authored tasks. At each round, a shared VLM proposes executable world programs and evidence schemas; a deterministic physics engine freezes each valid world, simulates matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches, and synthesizes discrete, answer-bound visual tasks. Exact verifier feedback from task solving updates both the shared policy via GRPO and an adaptive curriculum over physical intents. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct,  achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data, improving PhysBench Throwing by 8.8 points and ContPhy Counterfactual Removal and Goal-Pit by 7.4 and 24.4 points. These gains concentrate on interaction-sensitive and altered-world questions, demonstrating zero-shot transfer of causal principles to unseen complex dynamics (cloth, fluid, soft bodies) and real-world video.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Модель учится физике сама, проверяя себя движком
ru.desc: Статья представляет Physevolve, фреймворк самоэволюции для обучения vision-language моделей (VLM) каузальному физическому рассуждению без человеческих размеченных данных. Модель сама предлагает исполняемые программы миров, а детерминированный физический движок проверяет их и генерирует контрфактические сценарии, например, с удалённым телом. Точная обратная связь от верификатора обновляет политику через GRPO и адаптивный учебный план по физическим интентам. Метод, стартующий с Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, даёт заметный прирост на PhysBench, CausalPhys и ContPhy и переносится на ткань, жидкости, мягкие тела и реальные видео.

en.title: Empowering VLMs with Self-Generated Physics for Causal Reasoning
en.desc: Physevolve is a framework that enhances vision-language models (VLMs) for understanding physical reasoning by using a physics engine to create and validate simulated environments. It allows models to generate their own training scenarios, overcoming the limitations of traditional datasets that lack counterfactual examples. By simulating both factual and counterfactual outcomes, the framework provides a reliable source of truth for training VLMs on dynamic interactions. The results show significant improvements in performance on various benchmarks, demonstrating the model's ability to apply causal reasoning to complex physical scenarios without needing human-generated data.

zh.title: 自我演变的因果推理模型
zh.desc: Physevolve 是一种训练视觉-语言模型的方法，专注于因果物理推理。它利用物理引擎验证模型自生成的可执行世界和反事实模拟，从而在没有人类数据的情况下提高动态基准的表现。通过自我演变的框架，模型能够构建自己的训练问题，并在每一轮中生成可执行的世界程序和证据模式。最终，Physevolve 在多个基准测试中取得了显著的性能提升，展示了因果原则在复杂动态和真实视频中的零样本迁移能力。

papers.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching
papers.abstract: Abstract MoveBench introduces a specialized benchmark for evaluating large language models on sports and health coaching, emphasizing safety, scientific validity, and personalization across multiple-choice and open-ended tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their deployment in the sports and health domain remains high-risk due to the absence of domain-specific evaluation benchmarks. Existing general-purpose benchmarks (e.g., MMLU and HELM) primarily assess broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but fail to capture critical domain requirements such as exercise safety, physiological appropriateness, personalization, and actionable coaching quality. This gap is particularly concerning in fitness and health applications, where incorrect or unsafe recommendations can lead to physical harm. To address this limitation, we introduce MoveBench, the first comprehensive benchmarking framework specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching. The proposed benchmark integrates heterogeneous task formats, including multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and open-ended question answering (OpenQA), grounded in real-world user scenarios and paired with structured rubrics emphasizing safety compliance, scientific validity, and training logic. Through large-scale evaluation of 15 diverse LLMs on 809 questions with 5,012 rubric-level criteria, our results reveal substantial performance variability, particularly in safety awareness, structured program design, and personalization capability, highlighting a critical gap between knowing and doing. Our work establishes a foundational evaluation standard for sports and health LLM applications and provides a reproducible framework for advancing safe, reliable, and context-aware AI-driven coaching systems. Open resources are available at https://github.com/SatoSakula/MoveBench.

ru.title: Знать не значит уметь: новый стандарт проверки AI-тренеров
ru.desc: Статья представляет MoveBench — первый специализированный бенчмарк для оценки LLM в сфере спорта и тренировок, где цена ошибки высока из-за риска травм. Существующие общие тесты вроде MMLU и HELM измеряют широкие знания и рассуждения, но не учитывают безопасность упражнений, физиологическую уместность и персонализацию. Бенчмарк объединяет вопросы с выбором ответа и открытые вопросы на основе реальных пользовательских сценариев, оценивая их по структурированным рубрикам из 5012 критериев. Эксперименты на 15 моделях выявили значительный разброс качества, особенно в понимании безопасности и построении программ, что указывает на разрыв между знанием и практическим применением.

en.title: MoveBench: Elevating AI Coaching Standards in Sports and Health
en.desc: MoveBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) specifically in the context of sports and health coaching. It addresses the lack of domain-specific evaluation tools that ensure safety, scientific validity, and personalization in coaching recommendations. The benchmark includes various task formats, such as multiple-choice questions and open-ended responses, to assess LLMs against real-world scenarios. Results from testing 15 LLMs reveal significant differences in their ability to provide safe and personalized coaching, highlighting the need for improved standards in AI-driven health applications.

zh.title: 运动与健康指导的智能评估新标准
zh.desc: MoveBench是一个专门用于评估大型语言模型在运动和健康指导领域表现的基准测试框架。它强调安全性、科学有效性和个性化，涵盖多项选择题和开放式问题等多种任务格式。现有的通用基准测试无法满足运动和健康领域的特定需求，可能导致不安全的建议。通过对15种不同的大型语言模型进行大规模评估，MoveBench揭示了在安全意识、结构化程序设计和个性化能力方面的显著性能差异。

papers.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
papers.abstract: Abstract GeoUG improves spatial reasoning by combining depth and multi-view generation with adaptive geometric verification during inference.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Second, we introduce 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing selected 2D cues, and find that generated depth provides larger reasoning gains on questions requiring fine-grained geometric discrimination. Building on this finding, we develop adaptive interleaved reasoning, in which GeoUG first drafts an answer and then decides whether to generate geometric evidence to confirm or revise it. We train this decision through reinforcement learning, balancing accuracy gains over retaining the draft against generation cost. GeoUG achieves circular accuracies of 97.9%, 90.8%, and 94.2% on CV-Bench-3D, 3DCueBench, and DA-2K with fewer generation calls than always generating.

ru.title: Сначала черновик, затем геометрическая проверка: генерация глубины помогает ИИ лучше понимать пространство
ru.desc: Статья представляет GeoUG — унифицированную модель, которая объединяет генерацию глубины и многовидовых изображений с пониманием пространственных отношений. Авторы вводят multi-scale depth codec на основе предобученного visual autoencoder для генерации metric depth и показывают, что совместное обучение улучшает spatial understanding. Для контроля сложности предложен бенчмарк 3DCueBench, на котором генерируемая глубина дает наибольший прирост в задачах тонкого геометрического различения. Модель использует adaptive interleaved reasoning: сначала строит черновой ответ, затем через reinforcement learning решает, стоит ли генерировать геометрические доказательства, балансируя точность и стоимость генерации.

en.title: Enhancing Spatial Reasoning with GeoUG
en.desc: GeoUG is a model designed to enhance spatial reasoning by integrating depth and multi-view generation with geometric verification during inference. It employs a multi-scale depth codec that utilizes a pretrained visual autoencoder to generate metric-depth, improving spatial understanding through joint training. The model also introduces 3DCueBench to manage geometric complexity while optimizing 2D cues, leading to better performance on tasks requiring detailed geometric reasoning. Additionally, GeoUG uses adaptive interleaved reasoning, where it drafts answers and selectively generates geometric evidence, achieving high accuracy with fewer generation calls through reinforcement learning.

zh.title: GeoUG：提升空间推理的新方法
zh.desc: GeoUG是一种改进空间推理的模型，它结合了深度生成和多视角生成，并在推理过程中进行自适应几何验证。该模型通过几何监督和显式几何证据来增强空间理解能力。我们设计了一个多尺度深度编码器，利用预训练的视觉自编码器生成度量深度，并通过联合训练提高空间理解的效果。此外，GeoUG采用自适应交错推理，首先草拟答案，然后决定是否生成几何证据来确认或修正答案，从而在生成成本和准确性之间取得平衡。
